children: Norway’s trade surplus widened sharply to NOK 100.4 billion in August 2026 from NOK 59.3 billion in the same month a year earlier.

This marked the largest surplus since January 2023, as exports jumped by 32.9% year-on-year to NOK 191.0 billion, mainly driven by higher shipments of food and live animals (+11.2%), fuels and lubricating oils, and electric power (+51.9%), animal and vegetable oils, fats, and waxes (+20.5%), and processed goods grouped mainly by material (+14.0%).

Meanwhile, imports rose by 7.3% to NOK 90.6 billion, lifted by increased purchases of raw materials (non-edible), except fuels (+36.5%), fuels and lubricating oils, and electric power (+68.6%), machinery and means of transport (+2.7%), and different finished products (+0.7%).

For the January–August period, the country posted a trade surplus of NOK 608.9 billion, compared to NOK 489.6 billion, up 24.4% from the corresponding month of the previous year, as export growth (11.7%) far outpaced imports (3.1%).

title: Norway Trade Surplus Hits Three-Year High
